stories.body: Donald Trump said renewed US attacks on Iran were highly unlikely after meeting Qatar’s prime minister in Washington on Monday, while maintaining that American forces remained ready to act. He said Gulf allies favored keeping the naval blockade of Iranian ports in place, and Qatar’s leader described their discussions about a settlement as positive. Iranian officials disputed Trump’s account of negotiations, although President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran remained open to talks without coercion. The comments follow Republican midterm losses that senior party figures have linked to the war. No agreement ending the conflict was announced.
stories.headline: Trump calls further US strikes on Iran unlikely, but blockade continues

stories.body: Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first trilateral talks since February. US officials said both sides had privately shown some flexibility over territory, but stressed that territorial compromises depended on an agreed postwar security framework. Proposals include guarantees for Ukraine, security consultations, crisis hotlines and reciprocal measures to reduce tensions. Kyiv and Moscow remain publicly divided over Russian demands for Ukrainian-held territory in Donetsk. European leaders are pressing for a place in discussions that could reshape the continent’s security, while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio cautioned that a settlement remained some way off.
stories.headline: Ukraine peace talks resume with security guarantees at the center

stories.body: Donald Trump said the FBI was examining Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom US intelligence officials reportedly suspect of working for China. Trump said he believed Jensen Huang’s statement that he had been unaware of any alleged intelligence ties; the FBI declined to comment. Nvidia’s board has commissioned an independent investigation and said it had no reason to believe company secrets or national security had been compromised. China rejected the espionage allegations. Nvidia shares fell more than 4% on Monday, and a proposed shareholder class action accused the company and its chief executive of concealing the relationship.
stories.headline: Trump says FBI is examining Nvidia chief’s relationship with alleged Chinese spy

stories.body: France accused a cyber unit linked to Iran’s Revolutionary Guards of sabotaging supermarket refrigeration systems on October 11 and 12. Attackers remotely raised temperatures in some units above 50°C, spoiling large quantities of food and reportedly causing equipment damage and fires. French investigators identified the unit as Shahid Kaveh, citing technical evidence including Iranian IP addresses and the use of Farsi. Authorities opened a criminal investigation, summoned Iran’s ambassador and said they would seek European sanctions. Similar refrigeration failures have since been reported elsewhere in Europe, although the supplied reporting does not establish responsibility for those incidents.
stories.headline: France attributes supermarket refrigeration sabotage to Iranian cyber unit

stories.body: Fighting around Ethiopia’s Moyale area has displaced more than 50,000 people, according to a Kenya Red Cross regional official, although no final independently verified total is available. An earlier government-led assessment estimated nearly 36,000 displaced people, most staying with host families in Kenya. The violence stems from a longstanding land and administrative dispute between Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regions, with tensions escalating in October over regional flag displays. Arriving families lack food, bedding and shelter, and officials report continuing gunfire and health concerns. Kenya is working with UN agencies to register arrivals and mobilize assistance, but authorities said no emergency food stocks had been set aside for the sudden influx.
stories.headline: Ethiopian border violence drives tens of thousands into Kenya

stories.body: Republican Representative Thomas Massie introduced a resolution on Monday seeking to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, starting a 48-hour window for the House to take up the measure. Its eight articles allege unlawful conduct involving the Iran war, strikes on suspected drug boats and other military operations, alongside restrictions on press access. Lawmakers could vote on impeachment, refer the resolution to a committee or set it aside. Passage is considered unlikely while Republicans retain control until January, but Democratic leaders have signaled interest in pursuing Hegseth once they take over. Hegseth dismissed the effort, and Donald Trump reiterated his support for him.
stories.headline: Massie moves to force House action on Hegseth impeachment

stories.body: Donald Trump questioned the integrity of last week’s midterm elections in a Monday social media post, reversing his earlier acceptance of Democratic victories in both chambers of Congress. He cited polling errors, early voting totals and voting machines without providing evidence of fraud. The supplied reporting says pre-election surveys generally anticipated Democratic gains but understated their margins in many races. Trump had previously congratulated Democrats and expressed willingness to work with the incoming majorities. Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer criticized the renewed election denial, while some conservative figures also pushed back.
stories.headline: Trump questions midterm results after previously accepting defeat

stories.body: The Food and Drug Administration is requiring manufacturers of GLP-1 medicines to warn that the drugs can increase the risk of an eye stroke and potential vision loss, according to The Washington Post. The available article extract does not specify which medicines are covered or quantify the risk.
stories.headline: FDA requires GLP-1 drugmakers to warn about potential vision loss

stories.body: California voters rejected Proposition 40, a proposed one-time tax of 5% on billionaires’ net worth. Tech leaders spent hundreds of millions of dollars campaigning against the measure, according to France 24. Its defeat is a setback for progressive efforts to tax the wealth of the richest residents.
stories.headline: California rejects proposed one-time 5% billionaire wealth tax

stories.body: The Supreme Court allowed a major section of the Trump administration’s border security project in Texas to proceed, according to The Washington Post. The planned stretch extends more than 500 miles and includes a road, cameras, vehicle barriers and sensors in and around Big Bend National Park.
stories.headline: Supreme Court allows border security project around Big Bend

stories.body: Spain’s Ministry of Youth and Children has asked prosecutors to investigate TikTok after Maldita.es reported finding more than 1,000 items of explicit child sexual abuse material with a combined 48 million views. The investigation also identified accounts allegedly selling abuse material and failures in the platform’s reporting and moderation systems. Minister Sira Rego requested an urgent meeting with TikTok, and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said a suspension of the service was possible depending on the investigation’s findings. TikTok said it needed access to the full investigation to act. No suspension has been announced.
stories.headline: Spain considers suspending TikTok after child sexual abuse investigation

stories.body: Key physical evidence from the January 18 train crash at Adamuz, Córdoba, which killed 46 people, has spent months locked in a Transport Ministry room without being analyzed, El País reports. Rail sections and a suspect weld could help establish what caused the derailment, but nearly ten months later investigators have provided no conclusive explanation. The delays raise concerns for families seeking answers about the separate October 28 crash at Urda, Toledo, which killed 69 people and whose victims are being honored at a state funeral on Tuesday.
stories.headline: Evidence from fatal Adamuz train crash remains unexamined

stories.body: A judicial investigation into two Spanish intelligence officers accused of passing classified information to US intelligence services has concluded, bringing the case closer to trial in Madrid, according to El País. The officers were arrested in September 2023; one headed the CNI’s Russia unit, while the other held a more operational role. Both were initially detained on allegations of treason and disclosure of secrets before being released pending proceedings. They deny the accusations. The case would be an unusually rare Spanish prosecution of intelligence personnel for treason.
stories.headline: Investigation ends into Spanish intelligence agents accused of leaking to US

stories.body: Members of the Spanish neo-Nazi organization Núcleo Nacional received paramilitary training in Ukraine in August, according to court investigation documents reviewed by El País. The documents allege that members handled pistols and rifles without licenses and planned an armed uprising. The report follows 14 arrests last week in a police operation against the group. The allegations form part of an ongoing investigation led by a court in Gijón.
stories.headline: Spanish neo-Nazi group allegedly trained with firearms in Ukraine

stories.body: The Mossos d’Esquadra plan to deploy about 9,000 officers across four shifts for Wednesday’s general strike, 50% more than on a normal working day. Police expect serious disruption from around 6–7 a.m. on major roads and approaches to Barcelona, with possible incidents at logistics centers, industrial estates, ports and airports. A demonstration at Jardinets de Gràcia at 5:30 p.m. could attract more than 50,000 people and has received the force’s highest risk classification because of concerns about possible unrest. The operation begins at 10 p.m. Tuesday. Police advise checking travel conditions and allowing substantial extra time.
stories.headline: Wednesday’s general strike threatens major travel disruption across Catalunya

stories.body: Barcelona hotels received more than 7.1 million visitors in the first nine months of 2026, up 4.7% from a year earlier, according to city figures. September arrivals rose 5% to about 830,000, while overnight stays grew more slowly as average visits shortened. Travelers from outside the EU accounted for nearly 53% of hotel guests through September, with US arrivals approaching 1.2 million. Forward bookings point to a quieter finish to the year: November reservations were below last year’s level and December slightly above, although late bookings could change the picture. The tourism observatory put Barcelona’s average daily room rate for November through January at €224.
stories.headline: Barcelona hotel visitors rise 4.7%, with slower growth expected through year-end

stories.body: Active Airbnb listings in Barcelona have fallen by 20% in a year to just over 15,200, more than 4,000 fewer than twelve months earlier and the lowest total since 2015, according to city data reported by betevé. Deputy Mayor Laia Bonet attributed the decline to inspections and enforcement, saying the council flags about 300 illegal listings to Airbnb each month. The city wants the platform to prevent unlawful listings from appearing in the first place, a provision sought in an agreement that remains unsigned. Officials are also withdrawing tourist rental licenses from properties that fail to begin operating within the required period.
stories.headline: Barcelona Airbnb listings fall 20% to lowest level since 2015

stories.body: The loudest phase of construction on the L8 emergency shaft in Carrer de Muntaner is ending after crews completed its retaining walls on October 31. Workers have begun dismantling the large drilling machine and auxiliary installations, with removal expected by late November. Excavation will continue using smaller equipment that engineers say should cause less noise, and acoustic barriers will gradually come down. Two traffic lanes are expected to reopen early next year, although another closure will be needed later. Residents and businesses describe months of severe disruption, and substantial work remains before the tunnel boring machine reaches the shaft.
stories.headline: Muntaner’s L8 works move toward a quieter phase
